title: Perception gap video: replication, mechanism and persistence
rationale: In the source study the Perception gap video lowered the thermometer gap by 2.3 points (SE 0.997, n=641, p=0.021), one borderline result among 64 uncorrected tests. This follow-up replicates it at scale, tests whether correcting out-party misperceptions is the channel by comparing the full video with a version lacking the misperception data, and re-measures after about 2 weeks because the source only measured outcomes immediately.
contribution: Separates a replicated effect of the perception gap video from placebo and attention effects, tests whether the misperception correction carries it, and shows whether it persists.
limitations: Two-wave attrition may differ by arm
Online panel respondents may not represent the US public
Perceived out-party attitudes measured before and after may prime consistency
Effects are measured in survey outcomes, not behavior
Thermometers are collected as numeric text entries (0-100) rather than sliders

design.title: Perception gap video: replication, mechanism and persistence
design.overview: US Democrats and Republicans are randomized to one of four arms: the Perception gap video, the same video without the misperception data, a placebo video of matched length, or a control that says 'Please continue'. Perceived out-party attitudes are measured before and after exposure, then thermometers and support for undemocratic practices are measured. About 2 weeks later respondents are re-contacted and the outcomes are remeasured.
design.hypothesis: The full Perception gap video lowers the in-party minus out-party thermometer gap relative to control by about 1.4 points or more. The effect is mediated by reduced misperception of out-party attitudes, so the no-data variant has a smaller effect. Some of the effect remains at about 2 weeks. Undemocratic-practice support does not increase.
design.primaryOutcome: Affective polarization (in-party minus out-party thermometer) immediately after exposure, full video versus control.
design.comparison: Primary test: full Perception gap video versus control. Secondary: full video versus no-data variant (the correction), full video versus placebo, mediation by change in perceived out-party attitudes, wave 2 persistence, and support for undemocratic practices.
design.population: US adult Democrats and Republicans (including leaners) from a Lucid-style online panel.

assumptions: Power: about 1000 per arm to detect 1.4 points at 80% power (observed -2.3, SE 0.997 at n=641; true effect probably smaller; SD about 20 implied by SEs). Recruit about 4,000 to 4,800 allowing attrition; re-contact all about 2 weeks later.
One pre-registered primary test: full video vs control on post thermometer gap, adjusting for pre gap; others secondary with multiplicity correction.
Platform: Lucid-style panel; compensation per panel standard.
Mediator: perceived out-party attitudes is a single item; add more items if desired.
unresolved: Video files and the edited no-data version must be produced by the research team.
IRB approval number and compensation amount.
Wave 2 invitation mechanics and reminders are handled by the panel.
